pr_body:
Add a deprecation warning and a system property `es.cluster_health.request_timeout_200` to opt in for returning 200 which will be the default in 8.0.0

Fixes #70849
pr_title: Deprecate returning 408 for a server timeout on `_cluster/health`

review_comment: This returns `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` even if we didn't time out?
Yes, indeed, the check wasn't put correctly. I need to add a test that sets `es.cluster_health.request_timeout_408` to catch such mistakes.
++ I'd suggest adding another test to the `qa` project, that's generally the simplest way to control things like system properties.

I've decided to make the property as not static, so we can set in a constructor in `ClusterHealthResponsesTests`. It seems to much faster and easier to test this way instead of creating another full blown integration test. The test is called `testTimeoutReturns200IfOptedIn`

The trouble with this is that if the system property is invalid, it'll just make cluster health explode (with a `500 Internal Server Error`) on a timeout. We should be stricter and not even let the node start up in that case.

I'm ok with passing the flag into the response constructor for a unit test but I think we still have to parse the property up front while the node is initialising, and I would very much prefer to have an end-to-end test that the opt-in actually works.
